key_insight: Distal weight-bearing implants work best as integrated biomaterial-mechanical systems, where macro-geometry, graded Ti-HAp interfaces, and gait-phase loading must be co-designed for durable fixation.
engineering_relevance: For implant engineers, the main challenge is balancing distal support with reduced bending, shear, micromotion, and coating damage while still promoting reliable osseointegration.
method: Systematic review of DWBI design, biomaterials, and clinical translation literature
Quantitative trend analysis of 34 direct-contribution papers and 32 empirical studies
Synthesis of finite element analysis, functionally graded materials, and in-vivo evidence
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that more than half of the empirical evidence is still bench- or simulation-level, with animal and clinical validation forming a smaller portion of the dataset.
watch_item: Graded Ti-HAp and FGM concepts are promising, but much of the supporting evidence is indirect, so device-level fatigue, coating integrity, and patient-realistic validation remain unresolved.
paper_title: Biomaterials and biomechanical design of distal weight-bearing implants: Computational modeling, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
